proof.criterion: The tester's finding 1, and Sami's router design (dispatch://INFRA-490/comment/e0ed1a3b): a pull request runs only the jobs its change needs, so the ci-images job must not run on every change
proof.surface: ci.yaml as GitHub parses it, and the router's own checks, which are what decide whether a job runs
proof.command: bash .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.sh ; bash .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.test.sh ; bash .github/scripts/ci-ok.test.sh ; and a PyYAML parse of ci.yaml for the job's wiring
proof.observed: `every ci.yaml filter matches every file its job reads (25 gates)`, 24 before. The parse reads ci-images as `needs: changes`, `if: needs.changes.outputs.ci_images == 'true'`, in ci-ok's needs and with `"ci-images": "ci_images"` in its SELECTED_BY; ci_filter_coverage.py's ALWAYS_RUN is back to `("changes", "lint")` and ci-ok.sh is byte-identical to its pre-round-1 content. The gate is split by what each half reads: `check-ci-images.sh tree` prints `.github/ci-images.yaml holds 12 row(s); 35 reference(s) in 31 file(s) of CI's reach name one of those rows; of 6273 text file(s) swept, the 29 that name mirror.gcr.io are all in the exception list` and makes no network read, and `check-ci-images.sh package` prints `.github/ci-images.yaml holds 12 row(s), 12 of them in the package`. lint runs the tree half on every change, because a change that puts mirror.gcr.io back into a Go constant touches no file an image filter would name; ci-images runs the copy and then the package half, selected by its own filter.
proof.negativeControl: bash .github/scripts/check-ci-images.sh with no mode -> exit 1, `this check takes one mode: tree reads the files of this tree and makes no network read, and package reads ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion/ci`; the harness has a case for no mode and for both. Its case `each mode runs its own half` refuses a tree with a docker.io Go string under `tree`, with a spy on CI_IMAGES_MANIFEST_HEAD proving zero package reads, and passes the same tree under `package` with four package reads and no tree refusal. 82 assertions, 67 before.

proof.criterion: The tester's finding 1, second half — on a push to main that touches .github/ci-images.yaml, mirror-images.yaml and ci-images both ran the copy
proof.surface: The workflow files, and every file that named the deleted one
proof.command: grep -rIn 'mirror-images' over the tree ; bash .github/scripts/check-image-trigger-paths.sh ; bash .github/scripts/check-action-pins.sh ; a PyYAML parse of every workflow file
proof.observed: .github/workflows/mirror-images.yaml is deleted: ci.yaml runs on a pull request, a merge group and a push to main, so the ci-images job covers every event that can bring a new row, and one copy path is the whole of it. A failed copy is re-run with `gh run rerun`, as any job is. grep finds the name nowhere; the files that carried it are corrected (.github/ci-images.yaml, mirror-ci-images.sh, check-ci-images.sh's messages, check-bun-version.sh, ci.yaml's comments, AGENTS.md, .dispatch/architecture/release-engineering.md, the INFRA-567 solution page, rig.sh). Every workflow parses, every action is pinned, and every image trigger still covers every input its build reads (5 image builds). 58 job definitions, 5 reusable-workflow calls, every other carrying a timeout-minutes.
proof.negativeControl: check-ci-images.sh's own staleness rule is the control that the deletion did not leave a lie behind: an EXCEPTIONS entry naming a file the tree no longer holds, or a reach file that is gone, fails the check, and the tree half passes.

proof.criterion: Spec version 6 from dispatch://INFRA-318 — a workflow runs the scripts/e2e proofs on a GitHub-hosted runner, the tester's finding 2
proof.surface: GitHub Actions in sjawhar/legion: the `e2e` label on this pull request
proof.command: The E2E proofs workflow: run 40957651922 at a744ce61, then run 40966595125 at 4d8ae1f7 after the fix that run found
proof.observed: Run 40957651922 settled and did its job, which is to find what a reading of the scripts cannot: `stage1-skeleton` and `dispatch-claimant-delivery` passed, and the three proofs that start the Go daemon failed at one line, read from the evidence artifact each job uploaded: `the daemon exited before it answered /healthz: missing required daemon tools: jj (set LEGION_JJ_PATH to an absolute executable path)`. The job gave them no jj. .github/e2e-scripts.json now marks the three rows that start the daemon and the job installs the jj the worker image ships for those rows alone. Run 40966595125 is that head's run. The artifacts themselves are the second half of the acceptance and they worked: `gh run download 40957651922 --name e2e-merged-root-waits-40957651922-1` gave transcript.log, proof.log, daemon.log, nats.log and output.log, which is how the cause was read.
proof.negativeControl: The run itself was the control: three of five proofs failed, each naming its cause, so the workflow reports a failing proof rather than passing it. The select job's refusal path is the other: a workflow_dispatch naming a script of the `elsewhere` list fails with what that script's own header needs, and a script in neither list fails the run.

proof.criterion: The tester's finding 3 — the pull request body's cache figures did not reconcile with the tree or with each other
proof.surface: The measurement itself, repeated in this pod, and every file that carries a figure
proof.command: Fill a scratch GOMODCACHE the way worker.Dockerfile's go stage fills it (`go mod download` over go.work from packages/daemon), then du -sh, du -sb, and a count of the module zips
proof.observed: The download cache the image copies is 380 MiB by `du -sh`, 392,260,597 bytes apparent, over 419 module zips, and holds 3,337 files of every kind, the .lock files and sumdb/ among them. The whole module cache, the extracted module trees included, is 2.2 GiB, and the image carries the download half alone. Every figure in packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile, docs/kubernetes.md and the pull request body is now exactly that, the 2.2 GiB is named as the whole cache rather than as the trees, and the file count is dropped rather than published: it is the one figure a reader cannot reproduce from what the image carries, which is why the tester and I measured it differently.
proof.negativeControl: The tester's own five counts of the same directory (3,325; 2,906; 2,869; 2,450; 2,031) against my 3,337 are the control: a file count of a module cache depends on what the counter excludes, so no single one is reproducible, and the two figures that both of us reproduce exactly, 380 MiB and 419 zips, are the ones published.

filesChanged: .github/scripts/check-ci-images.sh: one required mode, tree or package, with the header's refusal list split between them
.github/scripts/check-ci-images.test.sh: every case under the mode that owns it, a case per mode on the real tree, a case for no mode and for both, and a case proving each mode runs its own half
.github/workflows/ci.yaml: lint runs the tree half; ci-images is an ordinary router job with its own ci_images filter and output, and runs the copy then the package half
.github/scripts/ci_filter_coverage.py, ci-ok.sh, ci-ok.test.sh, ci_job_reads.py: ALWAYS_RUN back to changes and lint, and the ci_images gate wired the ordinary way
.github/workflows/mirror-images.yaml: deleted, with every file that named it corrected
.github/e2e-scripts.json and .github/workflows/e2e.yaml: the rows that start the daemon get jj
packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile and docs/kubernetes.md: one cache figure, 380 MiB over 419 module zips, with the 2.2 GiB named as the whole module cache
deviations: mirror-images.yaml is deleted rather than kept with workflow_dispatch alone, which the architect left to me. With ci-images selected on a pull request, a merge group and a push to main by the same paths, a workflow_dispatch-only file would be a second way to do one thing with no caller, and a failed copy is re-run with gh run rerun like any job.
openQuestions: E2E proofs run 40966595125 at this head, the run that carries the jj fix, had not settled when this phase completed. The run before it, 40957651922, is the evidence that the workflow runs the proofs and reports a failure with its cause and its artifacts; this one is the evidence that all five pass. The tester reads it with `gh run view 40966595125` and `gh run download 40966595125`.

Docs (main) run 40946334589 on scratch pull request #2520 is still pending in the `pages` concurrency group, where main's own runs are pending too. It would show docs-site.yaml's upload-pages-artifact step and docs-pages.yaml's deploy job skipping on a branch. #2520 stays open until it settles, because closing it would cancel the only surface that step has before the merge.
discoveredComplexity: A reading of a live proof's header does not tell you what its binaries need: all three live-daemon-proof scripts name go and awk alone, and the daemon they start refuses to boot without jj. Only the run found it, which is the argument for the workflow this issue adds.
